questions.ask: Could you please tell me your date of birth?
Could you please tell me the last four digits of the mobile number we have on file for you?

hints.day_month_swapped: I think the day and the month may be the wrong way round. Could you say your date of birth again, with the month as a word?

intents.hardship: Financial difficulty, for example job loss, illness or bereavement.
intents.restructure: The customer asks for a reduced plan.
intents.human: The customer asks for a person.

lines.opening: Hello, this is Harbour Bank's virtual assistant, and we record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I am Harbour Bank's virtual assistant.
lines.scam: I understand your caution. You can always call Harbour Bank back on the number on our official website.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can explain once I have confirmed I am speaking with the right person.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share that information.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand, this will only take a moment.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach them?
lines.tp_ask_time: What time would suit, between 12 noon and 8 pm?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, I can only arrange a call back later today or on the next business day, between 12 noon and 8 pm. What time would suit?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share any details.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you, we will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry for the trouble, and thank you for letting me know.
lines.condolence: I'm very sorry for your loss, and I'm sorry to have troubled you.
lines.id_intro: Before we go on, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_why: These questions protect your privacy and make sure I only speak with the right person.
lines.id_explain: I need to confirm your identity before I can tell you why I'm calling.
lines.id_declined: I understand. Without these answers I can't go on with this call.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Could you say it again?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't confirm your identity on this call. Please contact us through online banking.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you. I'm calling about a missed payment.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has arrears of {amount}, and it is {days} days late.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full {amount} today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay the full amounts today?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, the lowest amount I can accept is {floor}. Could you manage that?
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, I can't accept that amount.
lines.date_past: That date has already passed. Which date would work for you?
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day. The next business day is {date}.
lines.after_deadline: I'm afraid the latest date I can accept is {date}.
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day would that be?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: To repeat, could you pay {amount} by {date}?
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can accept is {date}.
lines.confirm_q: Shall I go ahead and log that?
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise is recorded.
lines.sms_line: You'll get an email confirmation shortly.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, our system could not save that promise, so it has not been recorded.
lines.paid_line: Thank you. Payments can take up to three working days to reach your account.
lines.dispute_line: Thank you for telling me, I won't ask you for a payment today.
lines.hardship: I'm sorry to hear that. Would you like me to put you through to our Customer Care team?
lines.restructure_line: I'll put you through to our team who handle payment plans.
lines.human_ask_help: Is there anything I can help you with myself?
lines.transfer: I'm transferring you now, please hold.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change that promise on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Shall I go ahead and log that, yes or no?
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book that call back.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system is not responding right now.

assumptions: The memo of 25 September 2026 beats policy v4.2 section 7 where they disagree, as the cover email says.
Memo 1 beats 7.3: the second security question is the last four digits of the mobile number (tool field mobile_last4), not the postcode. The first question is date of birth (tool field dob).
Memo 2 beats 7.4: two wrong answers in total end the check, not three. The tool API summary still says three, but the brief wins.
Memo 3 beats 7.7: the latest promise date is the 10th business day after today, not 14 calendar days after.

Memo 4 adds lateness bands: up to 30 days late gets one attempt (full arrears by the deadline). More than 30 days late gets a second attempt (the minimum amount by the deadline). The first band starts at 0 and the second has an open upper bound of 100000.
Memo 5 extends 7.5: callbacks can be booked today or on the next business day, 12:00 to 20:00, strictly after now, with two asks in total.
The brief names no currency, so the default 'dollars' is used.
The minimum acceptable amount (floor) is the account field monthly_payment for every product type, called the contractual monthly payment.
The brief does not say whether the first full-arrears ask is for today or by the deadline, so the default 'today' is used.
add_note is not required by brief D, so notes are disabled and every note value is empty.
The confirmation question 'Is this {title} {last_name}?' and the read-back question 'Shall I go ahead and log that?' are used word for word from the brief.
The brief requires stating that the call is recorded. The opening says 'we record this call' (active voice).
After a recorded promise the agent says 'You'll get an email confirmation shortly.' (7.11).
The brief does not say how 'next Friday' is read, so the default 'following_week' is used.
The brief does not say how a numbers-only date is read. The materials use day-month style ('2 October 2026'), so 'dmy' is used.

The brief gives no wording for the tool's only hint value 'day_month_swapped'. The hint line says the day and month may be swapped and asks the customer to repeat the date of birth with the month as a word, so the next answer can be read without doubt. It does not mention the debt.
The brief does not say how many 'I don't want to talk' replies end the call, so the default of 2 is used.
The brief does not say whether a promise can be changed, so promise_change says it cannot be changed on this call.
The brief does not say whether to ask 'anything else' after a promise, so the default (one more turn) is used.
The brief does not say whether a same-day callback must fall on a business day, so business_days_only is false.
Promise dates must be business days, so a deadline that is not a business day moves to the previous business day.
Customers are behind on one product only. Multi-product settings keep their defaults and are not used in practice.
The system-failure rule is 'fails twice, then apologise and close with NP-SYS'. This maps to the service_error event.
Already paid uses the PD code (outcome paid, no reason). Dispute uses NP-DIS with no promise.

Requests for a reduced plan go to queue 'plans' (TR-PLAN). Requests for a person go to queue 'agents' (TR-AGT) after asking once whether the agent can help. Hardship accepted goes to queue 'care' (TR-CARE); declined closes with NP-HARD.
